whatItFakes: With fast-forward on (development only), a world campaign takes its turns four times as far apart, so a race is decided on fewer impressions than a played one.
why: The owner asked for 20 years in seconds, accepted if the result makes sense in the end (Nov 8, 1:58 a.m.); a campaign's town halls, speeches and doors are most of an election year's time.
replacement: A stride engine that steps the whole day loop in months for people nobody is watching; the campaign then reads the aggregate effect of its spending and reach.

whatItFakes: A full person nobody watches who hears a world candidate's speech takes the mean shift of their group of like hearers (place, lean, age band, how readily they yield), weighed by the members' mean closeness to the speaker, instead of their own; one who joins a group later takes its mean so far, and a grouped hearer does not weigh retelling it at home.
why: Owner, Nov 9: "not to track everything at every day"; the level-of-detail design (docs/speed/off-screen-campaigns-as-results.md, stage 1 step 1). Per-listener speech delivery was most of a campaign event's cost.
replacement: Opening a grouped hearer builds their own detail (that they came, what they heard) from the group's result and the record ids (step 3), and a household retelling read by group.
